svg.title: Typical positioning accuracy by method, from best to worst
svg.desc: Horizontal bar chart on a logarithmic scale. Real-time kinematic GPS: a few centimetres. Ultra-wideband: 10 to 30 centimetres. Wi-Fi RTT: 1 to 2 metres. GPS signal in space, government commitment: 2.0 metres or better, 95 percent of the time. GPS-enabled smartphone under open sky: 4.9 metres.
svg.text: How accurate is each way of knowing where you are?
Typical accuracy by method. Bars on a logarithmic scale; labels give the published range, not a single promise.
Sources: GPS.gov, “GPS Accuracy” (smartphone 4.9 m under open sky; signal-in-space commitment ≤ 2.0 m user range error,
95% of the time; high-end dual-frequency/augmentation users reach a few centimetres); Android Developers, “Wi-Fi location:
ranging with RTT” (typically 1–2 m); FiRa Consortium / IEEE 802.15.4z literature (UWB 10–30 cm). Real-world accuracy
varies with surroundings; bars are drawn on a log scale from the midpoint of each published range.
